title: Gift cards for less than face value
description: Website lets you bid on gift-cards for fractions of their value.

asr.full_text: Now, are you the type of person who likes buying gift cards for other people? It turns out you don't have to pay full price for one. Smart Shopper Daphne Monroe shows you how to get a $50 gift card for, get this, just $10. How would you like to win a $50 gift card for under $10? Sounds too good to be true. But it's not. I did it. It's a website called DFWBid.com. And you bid on gift cards valued at $50 or more in increments of just one penny at a time. Here's how it works. You sign up and buy credits. You need three credits to join an auction and three credits will cost you three bucks. The auctions are at eight o'clock Arizona time every night and it's actually kind of fun. You bid in increments of pennies and the longest an auction can last is one hour. So if you win, you'll definitely be getting a deal. There are normally two auctions going on and there are tons of gift cards to choose from. Walmart, Visa, even dining cards. Each time someone bids, the clock is reset for a minute. And 15 seconds. But there's another way to win. It's called the Penny Buy feature. During the. Auction, the Penny Buy is active for just five minutes. If you click on it and it's active,. You have to answer two really simple questions, like two plus two. If you're first to answer the. Questions right, you win the gift card for one penny and the auction ends. But you will have to. Pay $4.99 for shipping. I have to say I was kind of skeptical of this website at first,. But you know what? I actually won and I received my $50 Target gift card and I went to Target. And it was valid. So it definitely works. Now do keep in mind that this $50 gift card. Cost me a total of $8. So it was $4.99 for shipping plus $3 to join the auction. Of course,. You can't forget the penny to actually win the auction. And if you don't win, you will be out those $3. So do keep that in mind before signing up. I'll have all the information on our website at abc15.com and click on the Smart Shopper section. I'm Daphne Monroe, your Smart Shopper.

textual.observation: The speaker promotes a website auction in which viewers buy credits and bid for a claimed $50 gift card at a substantially lower total cost, with a separate shipping payment.

evidence.quote: Smart Shopper Daphne Monroe shows you how to get a $50 gift card for, get this, just $10.
You sign up and buy credits. You need three credits to join an auction and three credits will cost you three bucks.
If you're first to answer the. Questions right, you win the gift card for one penny and the auction ends. But you will have to. Pay $4.99 for shipping.
And if you don't win, you will be out those $3.

textual.context: Presented as a Smart Shopper segment and personal account; the speaker describes the website and encourages viewers to sign up, while also stating that participants can lose the auction-entry fee.
textual.potential_relevance: The unusually low-value gift-card outcome is directly tied to signing up, purchasing credits, bidding, and paying shipping, with a stated loss if the viewer does not win; these combined claims and conditions may require later context assessment.
textual.limitations: These records do not independently establish whether the website, gift cards, auction results, fees, or stated savings are genuine or representative.

visual.observation: A webpage displays gift cards with a stated retail price of $50.00 and a current price of $0.21, alongside visible "Bid Now" and "Penny Buy" controls; another sampled state shows a gift card marked "Closed" with a "Winning Price" of $0.01.
visual.context: The material appears within a televised consumer-shopping segment and shows a website interface demonstrating an auction or purchase process; the sampled frames do not establish whether the offer is being promoted, reported on, or demonstrated as an example.
visual.potential_relevance: The displayed low-price gift-card outcome is linked to visible bidding or penny-purchase actions, creating a reward/return claim connected to a money-related requested action that may merit review in context.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish the site's legitimacy, any required fees or payment flow beyond the visible controls, whether a viewer completed a transaction, or whether the displayed prices and winner information were genuine.

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker expresses initial skepticism but then presents a personal claim of winning and receiving a valid gift card.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as an ABC 15 "Smart Shopper" consumer segment demonstrating a gift-card auction. It explains the required credits and warns that a participant who does not win loses the $3 entry fee, while the low displayed prices and auction interface are presented as part of the demonstration rather than an unexplained money-making claim.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary context is an ordinary rewards and promotion segment centered on obtaining gift cards below their retail value through a described auction and Penny Buy process. The segment also discloses the required credit payment, shipping payment and possible loss when an auction is not won.
